questions.passage:
A hospital's quality improvement data shows:
- Patient falls decreased by 45% after introducing bed sensors
- Pressure injuries fell 30% after turning schedules were enforced
- Hospital-acquired infections dropped 25% after hand hygiene audits began
- Medication errors remained unchanged throughout the period
questions.question: Which inference is best supported?
options: All patient safety issues have been resolved
Targeted interventions appear effective for specific safety issues, but medication errors need different approaches
Medication errors are not a patient safety concern
Hand hygiene audits were the most effective intervention
questions.correct: Targeted interventions appear effective for specific safety issues, but medication errors need different approaches
questions.explanation: Three specific interventions each reduced their target issue (falls -45%, pressure injuries -30%, infections -25%), but medication errors stayed the same, suggesting different approaches are needed for that problem.

questions.passage: All patients referred to the oncology unit have abnormal blood markers. Some patients with abnormal blood markers require biopsy. All patients who have a biopsy need post-procedure observation.
questions.question: Which conclusion definitely follows?
options: All oncology patients have a biopsy
Some oncology patients may need post-procedure observation
All patients needing observation are in oncology
questions.correct: Some oncology patients may need post-procedure observation
questions.explanation: Oncology referral → abnormal blood markers. Some abnormal markers → need biopsy. Biopsy → post-procedure observation. So some oncology patients may need post-procedure observation.

questions.passage:
A dental clinic tracks appointment no-shows:

| Day | Booked | Attended | No-Show |
|-----|--------|----------|--------|
| Monday | 30 | 24 | 6 |
| Tuesday | 35 | 30 | 5 |
| Wednesday | 25 | 22 | 3 |
| Thursday | 40 | 30 | 10 |
| Friday | 20 | 18 | 2 |
questions.question: Which day has the highest no-show rate as a percentage of booked appointments?
questions.explanation: Monday: 6/30=20%. Tuesday: 5/35=14.3%. Wednesday: 3/25=12%. Thursday: 10/40=25%. Friday: 2/20=10%. Thursday has the highest no-show rate at 25%.

questions.passage: Should hospitals be required to publicly report individual surgeon complication rates?
questions.question: Which is the strongest argument AGAINST public reporting?
options: It may discourage surgeons from performing high-risk but necessary procedures, harming patients who need them
Some patients may not understand the statistics
Surgeons may feel stressed by being monitored
The data collection process is time-consuming
questions.correct: It may discourage surgeons from performing high-risk but necessary procedures, harming patients who need them
questions.explanation: This raises a critical patient safety concern — if surgeons avoid complex cases to protect their statistics, patients needing those procedures suffer. This is a well-documented unintended consequence of public reporting.

questions.passage: Four medications — Amoxicillin, Ciprofloxacin, Diazepam, and Erythromycin — are stored in cabinets labelled 1, 2, 3, and 4. Amoxicillin is in a lower-numbered cabinet than Ciprofloxacin. Diazepam is not in cabinet 1 or 4. Erythromycin is in cabinet 4.
questions.question: In which cabinet is Amoxicillin?
questions.explanation: Erythromycin is in cabinet 4. Diazepam is not in 1 or 4, so Diazepam is in 2 or 3. Amoxicillin is lower-numbered than Ciprofloxacin. The remaining cabinets for Amoxicillin, Ciprofloxacin, and Diazepam are 1, 2, and 3. Amoxicillin must be in cabinet 1 (lowest of the available) and Ciprofloxacin in 2 or 3 (higher). With Diazepam filling the remaining spot, Amoxicillin must be in cabinet 1.

questions.passage: Of 200 patients at a diabetes clinic: 120 have Type 2 diabetes, 45 have Type 1 diabetes, 15 have both types (Type 1 with secondary complications mimicking Type 2), and 50 have gestational diabetes only.
questions.question: How many patients have Type 2 diabetes only (not Type 1)?

questions.passage: A rapid COVID test has a sensitivity of 80% and specificity of 98%. In a population where 5% are currently infected, 10,000 people are tested.
questions.question: How many total positive results will there be?
questions.explanation: Of 10,000: 500 are infected (400 true positives). 9,500 are not (190 false positives). Total positive = 400 + 190 = 590.

questions.passage: Should hospitals implement a policy requiring minimum staffing ratios for nursing wards?
questions.question: Which is the strongest argument FOR minimum staffing ratios?
options: Evidence shows that nurse-to-patient ratios directly affect patient mortality, falls, and medication errors
Nurses deserve to have manageable workloads for their own wellbeing
Hospitals in other countries already use staffing ratios
Patients feel more comfortable when there are more nurses on the ward
questions.correct: Evidence shows that nurse-to-patient ratios directly affect patient mortality, falls, and medication errors
questions.explanation: This provides the strongest justification by linking staffing ratios directly to measurable patient safety outcomes. While nurse wellbeing and patient comfort are valid, the evidence-based patient safety argument is most compelling for policy.

questions.passage:
A rehabilitation centre tracks patient outcomes over 6 months:

| Month | Discharged | Improved but ongoing | No change | Deteriorated |
|-------|-----------|---------------------|-----------|-------------|
| Jan | 10 | 25 | 5 | 2 |
| Feb | 12 | 28 | 4 | 1 |
| Mar | 15 | 30 | 3 | 2 |
| Apr | 18 | 32 | 2 | 1 |
| May | 20 | 35 | 1 | 1 |
| Jun | 22 | 38 | 1 | 0 |
questions.question: What is the trend in patients showing no change over the six months?
questions.explanation: No change patients: Jan 5, Feb 4, Mar 3, Apr 2, May 1, Jun 1. This shows a consistent downward trend from 5 to 1.

questions.passage: Three specialists — Dr. Mia, Dr. Noah, and Dr. Olivia — consult on three consecutive days (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday). Dr. Mia consults before Dr. Olivia. Dr. Noah does not consult on Monday.
questions.question: On which day does Dr. Olivia consult?
questions.explanation: Dr. Noah not on Monday, so Noah is Tuesday or Wednesday. Dr. Mia before Dr. Olivia. If Noah is Tuesday: Mia is Monday, Olivia is Wednesday. If Noah is Wednesday: Mia is Monday, Olivia is Tuesday. Both arrangements are valid, so Olivia could be on Tuesday or Wednesday.
